<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/appendix/firmware-release-notes/ -->

# Firmware release notes

What changed in each firmware release, from the release notes in the firmware repository, up to the release this site describes.

## V108 (2026-08-26)

STEPFOC firmware **V108** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### Bug fixes
- Fixed calibration (`#Cal`) spuriously failing with `Phase order is wrong!` on otherwise-healthy motors. The "confirm commutation" pre-check (before the real angle-offset search) commands a pure torque-axis voltage using the not-yet-calibrated encoder angle — depending on a given unit's actual rotor-to-encoder mounting angle, that command could land almost entirely on the wrong axis and produce ~zero torque, failing the check even though nothing was actually broken. Bench-confirmed on a real unit.
- Fix: retry the pre-check once at a 90° angle bias before declaring failure — guaranteed to land within 45° of the true torque axis on at least one of the two tries. The downstream angle-offset search is unaffected and already independent of this pre-check.
- Added `Spin-confirm delta` / `Vbus` diagnostics to `#Cal`'s failure report, for the rare case both tries still fail.

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V108.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `25cbc4887ca2c192eba6e708930eb6b6c677fd1e76299313c3b3ce3459e0e8a1`
- Size: 99188 bytes

Built from commit 46b4911 on `bootloader-version`. Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V107 (2026-08-24)

STEPFOC firmware **V107** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### Bug fixes
- Fixed PD mode (`IN_DATA_PACK_PD` over CAN): the commanded speed was written into `Feedforward_speed`, but `PD_mode()` reads `Velocity_setpoint` for its KD term — so the KD (velocity-damping) term of the impedance controller was always evaluated against a stale/zero setpoint and had no effect. The CAN handler now writes the field the control law actually reads. `IN_DATA_PACK_1` / position mode is unaffected — `Feedforward_speed` there is correct and continues to feed the position cascade.

#### CAN bus
- Added a generic settings command (`IN_SETTINGS`) so future boolean settings don't each need their own command ID. Payload is `mask` + `value` (one byte each), one bit per setting — only bits set in the mask are applied, so a sender only needs to know about the bits it cares about.
- First setting on this command: brake vs. coast (bit 0), previously only selectable over UART (`Brake` / `Coast`), now selectable over CAN as well.

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V107.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `63699037c79318e1d78738edcb13e9f9bc00a3393dc5803f920b244a60622ae2`
- Size: 98972 bytes

Built from commit 04ec180 on `bootloader-version`. Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V106 (2026-07-05)

STEPFOC firmware **V106** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### CAN bus
- The controller now drains up to 8 CAN messages per pass instead of just 1, so short bursts (multiple commands sent back-to-back, or a busy multi-node bus) no longer silently drop messages once the 3-deep hardware FIFO fills.
- A CAN peripheral that fails to initialize no longer bricks the board — UART stays fully usable, only the CAN bus is skipped.

#### Safety
- Added a hardware watchdog (100ms). If the control loop ever stops running, the board resets instead of leaving the motor driven at a stale duty cycle.
- Fixed a bug where `Torque_mode` could silently overwrite your commanded Iq setpoint when clamping to the current limit — reading it back after clamping now shows what you actually asked for, and raising the current limit afterward immediately restores the original commanded torque instead of requiring the command to be resent.
- Fixed undefined behavior in a serial-protocol integer conversion (`fourBytesToInt`).
- Synced default configuration values that had drifted between two locations in the code, so a fresh `#Default` and a freshly-flashed board's built-in defaults now agree.

#### EEPROM / configuration integrity
- Added CRC validation over the saved configuration, split into two independent halves: **calibration data** (resistance, inductance, Kt/KV, angle offset, current-loop gains, etc.) and **settings** (PID tuning, limits, watchdog config, CAN ID, etc.).
- This means a corrupted save (e.g. from a power loss mid-write) is detected and safely defaulted instead of silently running with garbage values — and critically, a *future* firmware update that only adds a new setting can no longer wipe your calibration, since the two are validated independently.
- Boards upgrading from older, pre-CRC firmware keep their existing calibration automatically — no need to recalibrate after this update.
- A few unused slots were reserved in the calibration block for upcoming features (e.g. magnet alignment), so those can be added later without another migration.

#### Performance
- PWM output no longer re-resolves which timer/channel it's writing to on every single call (it was doing this 4x per control tick) — resolved once and cached, freeing up ISR headroom.
- Velocity calculation switched from a floating-point divide to an integer multiply.

#### Usability
- New `#Help` command — prints a summary of the available commands.
- Serial now responds with "Unknown command" for unrecognized input instead of silently ignoring it.
- Calibration now prints progress during the angle-offset search (previously up to ~40 seconds of silence that could look like the board had hung).
- `#Error` now also reports driver faults (undervoltage/thermal/overcurrent), not just the other error types.
- `#Info` now always reports live ISR execution time, useful for checking control-loop headroom on the bench.

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V106.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `bc061fb273e7c836e3180fa597ecd373e7e357b0eab9130b63a7fd19b70a6073`
- Size: 98940 bytes

Built from commit 661e7d3 on `bootloader-version`. Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V105 (2026-07-04)

STEPFOC firmware **V105** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### What's new
- Reversed stepper phase wiring now calibrates automatically — no more "switch phases and try again." The firmware detects the wiring and compensates it in software, so **all 8 phase-wiring permutations calibrate identically and symmetrically**.
- `#Info` now reports the firmware's own build version, so the version is correct immediately after flashing (no `#Default` needed).

#### Assets
- `stepfoc-firmware-V105.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `0d80ce3cf78109f6ff54697425ed475ffca4e97e220d72fe0823ce1bd60a4908`
- Size: 95924 bytes

Built from commit bda57d6 on `bootloader-version`. Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V103 (2025-12-28)

First stable release for public

## V102 (2025-12-28)

First official release for the public

## V101 (2025-09-29)

Initial fully functional release based on spectral micro firmware.

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/appendix/theory/ -->

# Theory corner

The control concepts behind the driver's modes, for readers who want to know why a setting does what it does.
Nothing here is needed to use the driver; the chapters say what to type.

## Field-oriented control of a stepper

A hybrid stepper is a two-phase synchronous motor with many pole pairs: 50 for a 1.8° motor, so one mechanical
revolution is 50 electrical cycles. A conventional stepper driver drives it blindly: it advances the current
pattern one step at a time and relies on the rotor following. The torque the rotor receives depends on the angle
between the stator field and the rotor, the *load angle*; it is largest a quarter of an electrical cycle ahead of
the rotor and zero when the two are aligned. Because the driver does not know where the rotor is, it keeps full
current in the coils at all times, so that even a badly placed field produces enough torque, and it still loses
steps when the load angle exceeds 90° electrical.

Field-oriented control (FOC) closes that gap with a measurement of the rotor angle. The encoder on the motor shaft
gives the mechanical angle $\theta$; with the pole pairs $p$ and the angle offset $\theta_0$ found by calibration,
the electrical angle is $\theta_e = p\,\theta + \theta_0$. The two coil currents $I_A$ and $I_B$ are transformed
into the rotor's frame of reference (the Park transform):

$$
I_d = I_A \cos\theta_e + I_B \sin\theta_e,\qquad
I_q = -I_A \sin\theta_e + I_B \cos\theta_e
$$

$I_q$, the *quadrature* current, is the part of the current that stands at right angles to the rotor field and
produces torque: $\tau = K_t\, I_q$. $I_d$, the *direct* current, is aligned with the field and produces none. Two
PI controllers regulate $I_q$ to the torque demand and $I_d$ to zero by choosing the voltages $U_q$ and $U_d$;
the inverse transform turns those into the two coil voltages, applied by PWM at 25 kHz. The loop runs at 6250 Hz.

The consequences are what makes a FOC stepper behave like a servo: the current is only what the torque needs, so
the motor runs cool and quiet; the field is always placed where it produces the most torque per ampere; and a
step is never lost, because the controller knows the rotor position at every instant and works from the error,
not from a count of pulses.

Calibration supplies the constants this needs. The pole pairs come from the step angle. The current loop gains
follow from the coil's resistance $R$ and inductance $L$ and the chosen bandwidth $\omega_c = 2\pi f_c$ (`#Cbw`):
$K_p = L\,\omega_c$ and $K_i = R\,\omega_c$ cancel the coil's electrical time constant and give a first-order
response at $f_c$. The angle offset is found by driving a current along the $d$ axis and reading where the rotor
settles. The velocity constant $K_V$ comes from the back-EMF the spinning motor generates, and the torque
constant follows from it: in SI units $K_t = 1/K_V$ (with $K_V$ in rpm/V, $K_t \approx 9.55/K_V$ Nm/A).

## The cascade of loops

Position, velocity and current are controlled by three loops nested inside one another:

$$
\text{position loop: } \omega_d = K_{pp}\,(\theta_d - \theta)
\qquad
\text{velocity loop: } I_{q,d} = K_{pv}\,(\omega_d - \omega) + K_{iv}\!\int(\omega_d - \omega)\,dt
\qquad
\text{current loop: } U_q = \text{PI}(I_{q,d} - I_q)
$$

The position loop is proportional: its output is a speed demand, limited by the velocity limit. The velocity loop
is a PI controller: its output is a current demand, limited by the current limit; the integral term removes the
steady-state error a load would otherwise leave. The current loop is the innermost and fastest. Each loop must be
slower than the one inside it, by a factor of five to ten, for the inner loop to look like an ideal actuator to the
outer one; that is why the loops are tuned from the inside out, and why a current loop bandwidth of 500 Hz leaves
room for a velocity loop of a few tens of hertz and a position loop below that.

A command picks where the cascade is entered: a current setpoint uses the current loop alone, a speed setpoint
the two inner loops, a position setpoint all three. The *feedforward* terms the CAN motion frames carry are added
to the demands rather than computed from an error: a speed feedforward is added to the position loop's output, a
current feedforward to the velocity loop's output. A host that knows the trajectory can command it directly and
leave the loops to correct what is left, which gives a faster, smoother response than letting the loops produce
the whole demand from the error.

An integrator accumulates error over time, and keeps accumulating while the output is at its limit; the overshoot
this causes when the limit is released is *windup*. The velocity loop's integrator is clamped to the velocity
limit, and `#Rstint` resets the integrators on every new setpoint, which suits a host that sends one setpoint
after another in large steps.

## Impedance control

Impedance control does not prescribe a motion or a force. It prescribes the *relation* between the two: how much
force the motor produces when it is displaced from its setpoint and how fast. The driver's PD mode implements a
spring and a damper around the setpoint:

$$
\tau = K_P\,(\theta_d - \theta) + K_D\,(\dot\theta_d - \dot\theta) + K_t\, I_{ff}
$$

with the stiffness $K_P$ in Nm/rad, the damping $K_D$ in Nm·s/rad, and a current feedforward $I_{ff}$ for a known
load such as gravity. The torque is produced by the current loop ($I_q = \tau / K_t$), which is what makes FOC a
prerequisite: a stepper driven blindly cannot produce a commanded torque.

Pushed off its setpoint by an external force $F$, the motor yields by $\Delta\theta = \tau_{ext}/K_P$ and pushes
back with that force; let go, it returns, with the damper settling the motion. A small $K_P$ makes a soft joint,
a large one a stiff joint; $K_D$ without $K_P$ is a pure damper. The setpoint can move, in which case the virtual
spring drags the rotor along a trajectory with a bounded force — the property legged robots, hand-guided arms and
anything that touches people or an uncertain environment need. The impedance loop is also what a position loop
is *not*: the position loop's integral action removes any steady-state deflection and so makes the joint as stiff
as the current limit allows, which is the right thing for a machine tool and the wrong thing for a leg.

The full impedance model includes an inertia term, $M\ddot\theta$; the driver, like most joint controllers, leaves
it out, so the apparent inertia is the motor's own.

## Admittance control

Admittance is the inverse relation: the controller measures the force and commands a motion,

$$
\dot\theta_d = \frac{\tau_{ext} - K\,(\theta - \theta_0)}{B}
$$

on top of a stiff position controller. It is the natural form for a machine that has a force sensor and a position
loop that cannot be made soft, such as an industrial arm; impedance control is the natural form for a machine whose
actuator is a torque source, such as a FOC motor. The driver has no force sensor and implements impedance; a host
that wants admittance behaviour can estimate the external torque from $K_t I_q$ minus the known load and command
positions accordingly, with the limits of that estimate (friction, cogging, the current loop's accuracy).

## Compliance and stiffness

Stiffness $K$ is the force per unit of displacement; compliance is its inverse, $C = 1/K$, the displacement per
unit of force. *Passive* compliance is in the mechanism — a spring, a flexible finger, a belt; *active* compliance
is in the controller — the impedance loop above. The driver offers three points on that scale: the position mode,
stiff up to the current limit; the PD mode, as stiff as $K_P$; and the current mode, which is no stiffness at all,
a torque source the host shapes as it likes.

The current limit `#Ilim` is a force limit in every mode: the largest torque the motor will produce before it
yields, whatever the loops ask. Set it for the motor's rating, and for the mechanism's.

## Which mode

| Mode | Behaviour under an external force | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Position | holds the position up to the current limit, then yields | positioning, machines, anything that must not deflect |
| Velocity | holds the speed up to the current limit | conveyors, wheels, spindles |
| PD (impedance) | deflects in proportion to the force, returns when released | legs, arms that touch things or people, hand guiding, teleoperation |
| Current (torque) | produces the commanded torque, moves as the load dictates | a host that closes its own loop, gravity compensation, force-limited pressing |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/terminology/ -->

# Glossary

**Activated**
:   A flag the driver keeps (`#Activate`, Send_gripper_data_pack). In gripper mode a move is carried out only while
    the gripper is activated.

**ADDITIONAL2**
:   A spare pin of the driver, usable as an analog input or a digital input/output. HALL mode homes the motor
    against a sensor wired to it.

**Angle offset** (theta offset)
:   The angle between the encoder's zero and the motor's electrical zero, found by calibration and stored. The
    driver needs it to place the current vector relative to the rotor.

**Back-EMF**
:   The voltage a turning motor generates in its own coils, proportional to speed. It opposes the supply, limits the
    top speed at a given voltage, and is what calibration measures to find KV, Kt and the flux linkage.

**Board ID**
:   The bootloader's own address, 0 to 13, stored in its configuration page. The firmware keeps it equal to the CAN
    node ID.

**Bootloader**
:   The program in the first 12 KB of the driver's flash on boards shipped with firmware 104 or newer. It starts the
    firmware, and loads a new firmware over UART or CAN. See [The bootloader](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/07-firmware/the-bootloader/).

**Calibration**
:   The routine (`#Cal`) that checks the magnet and the supply, takes the motor's resistance, inductance and pole
    pairs, computes the current loop gains, spins the motor in open loop to learn the wiring, finds the angle offset
    and measures Kt, KV and the flux linkage. Its result is kept with `#Save`.

**CAN ID** (node ID)
:   The address of the driver on the CAN bus, 0 to 15. It occupies bits 10 to 7 of the 11-bit CAN frame identifier;
    the command ID occupies bits 6 to 1 and the error bit is bit 0.

**CANvas**
:   Source Robotics' USB-to-CAN adapter. It appears as a serial port and speaks slcan, which `python-can` and Motor
    GUI use.

**Command ID**
:   The number, 0 to 63, in bits 6 to 1 of a CAN frame identifier that says which message the frame carries. The
    API reference lists every command ID.

**Commutation**
:   Placing the stator current so that it produces torque at the rotor's present angle. FOC does it continuously
    from the encoder angle and the angle offset; a conventional stepper driver does it blindly, step by step.

**Control mode**
:   What the driver is doing with the motor: idle, position, velocity, current, PD (impedance), voltage torque, open
    loop, HALL, gripper, or calibration. A command that carries a setpoint puts the driver in the matching mode.

**Current loop bandwidth** (`#Cbw`)
:   How fast the current loop follows a change of its setpoint, in Hz. Calibration computes the current loop gains
    from it and the motor's resistance and inductance; 500 Hz by default.

**Daisy chain**
:   Several drivers on one CAN bus and one supply, each driver's second CAN and power connector feeding the next.

**d-q frame**
:   The rotating frame of reference FOC works in: the q axis is at right angles to the rotor field and the current on
    it (Iq) produces torque; the d axis is along the field and its current (Id) produces none, so it is held at 0.

**Diametrical magnet**
:   A disc magnet whose poles are across its diameter, so the field turns with the shaft. The encoder needs this
    kind; an axially magnetised disc looks the same and does not work.

**EEPROM**
:   The non-volatile memory on the driver that holds the configuration and the calibration. `#Save` writes it,
    `#Default` restores the factory values.

**Encoder ticks**
:   The unit of position: the 14-bit magnetic encoder gives 16384 ticks per revolution of the motor shaft, counted
    over as many revolutions as the motor makes. Speed is in ticks per second.

**Error bit**
:   Bit 0 of every CAN frame identifier the driver sends: 1 while any error is active.

**Feedforward**
:   A term added to a loop's output from what is known in advance rather than from the error: the motion frames
    carry a speed and a current feedforward so a host that knows the trajectory can command it directly, leaving
    the loops to correct the rest.

**Field-oriented control** (FOC)
:   Controlling a motor by regulating the stator current as a vector in the rotor's frame, from a measurement of the
    rotor angle. On a stepper it replaces the fixed step currents with sinusoidal currents that follow the rotor,
    which gives smooth, quiet, efficient motion with no lost steps and a known position.

**Firmware release**
:   One build of the firmware, numbered 103, 104, 105, … and tagged `V103`, `V104`, … in the firmware repository.
    `#Info` prints the release a driver runs. This documentation describes one release; the version selector
    switches between them.

**Flux linkage**
:   The rotor's magnetic flux as seen by a coil, in weber; found by calibration from the back-EMF, together with
    KV and Kt.

**Gripper mode**
:   The driver running a gripper (`#Gripper 1`): jaw positions from 0 (open) to 255 (closed), a speed, a current
    limit that becomes the grip force, and object detection.

**HALL mode**
:   Homing against a sensor on ADDITIONAL2: the motor turns at a set speed until the sensor triggers, then holds
    the position reached.

**Heartbeat**
:   A frame (Respond_Heartbeat) the driver sends at a set interval so the host knows it is alive. Off by default.

**Iq, Id**
:   The two components of the motor current in the d-q frame: Iq produces torque, Id is normally held at 0. The
    current mode's setpoint and limit are Iq values.

**Impedance (PD) mode**
:   The control mode in which the driver behaves like a spring and a damper around a position setpoint, with the
    stiffness `KP` and the damping `KD`, plus a current feedforward.

**Kt, KV**
:   The motor's torque constant (torque per ampere) and velocity constant (speed per volt), found by calibration.
    Kt turns a current into an estimated torque; KV gives the top speed at a supply voltage.

**Microstepping**
:   Driving a stepper with intermediate current levels between full steps. Only the open-loop commands
    (`#gosteps`, `#microstep`) use it; under FOC the current follows the rotor continuously.

**Motor GUI**
:   Source Robotics' browser tool for the driver: tuning, plots and firmware updates over a serial or CAN adapter.

**Open loop**
:   Driving the motor as a plain stepper, without the encoder in the loop: `#Openloop`, `#gosteps`, and the
    open-loop spin of the calibration.

**Phase order**
:   How the stepper's two coils are connected to A+/A− and B+/B−. Firmware 105 and newer learns the wiring during
    calibration and compensates it; firmware 103 asks for the wires to be swapped when it is reversed.

**Pole pairs**
:   The number of electrical cycles per mechanical revolution: 50 for a 1.8° stepper, 100 for a 0.9° stepper. Set
    with `#PP` before calibration.

**Remote frame**
:   A CAN frame with the RTR bit set and no data: a request. The host asks for data with a remote frame under a
    command ID, and the driver answers with a data frame under the same ID.

**Spectral Micro**
:   Source Robotics' BLDC driver, STEPFOC's sister: similar hardware and firmware and practically the same
    commands, for three-phase brushless motors.

**Step angle**
:   The angle of one full step of a stepper: 1.8° for the common 200-step motor, 0.9° for a 400-step motor. It
    sets the pole pairs: 360 ÷ (4 × step angle).

**Termination**
:   The 120 Ω resistor the first and the last node of a CAN bus need. The switch on the driver turns it on.

**Vbus**
:   The supply voltage at the driver, measured and printed in mV. Outside the limits the driver raises a Vbus
    error.

**Watchdog**
:   A timer the driver resets with every valid CAN frame it receives. When it is set (Send_Watchdog) and runs out,
    the driver reports a watchdog error and stops.

# API reference

Every CAN message and every UART command of the firmware release this site describes, the defaults the firmware
starts with, the error flags, and the map from the Python library's calls to the messages they send.

## Where the facts come from

The command IDs, the frame lengths the firmware accepts, the responses it sends, the list of UART commands with
their kind (Set/Get, Get or action), their argument type, the mode each enters and what it prints, and the
defaults are read from the firmware's source at its release tag by `tools/sync_firmware.py` in the documentation
repository, and the pages are built from that at every build. The descriptions, units and byte layouts are
written by hand, and the build fails when they name a command the firmware does not have, or miss one it has, or
when a byte layout does not fit the frame. The firmware version is in the version box on the
[landing page](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/).

## Conventions

- **Bytes** are numbered from 0, the first byte on the bus (`data[0]`). Multi-byte values are **big-endian**: the
  most significant byte first. Floats are IEEE 754 single precision in 4 bytes.
- **Bits** inside a byte are numbered from the most significant bit: bit 7 is the first flag the firmware packs
  into the byte, bit 0 the last.
- **Encoder ticks**: 16384 per revolution; speeds in ticks per second; currents in mA; voltages in mV.
- UART command names are **case-sensitive** and spelled exactly as the firmware compares them.

## In the API reference

- [CAN protocol](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/): the identifier, the three kinds of message, every message by group
- [UART commands](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/): the syntax and every command by group
- [Defaults](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/defaults/)
- [Errors and LED states](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/errors/)
- [Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/python/): library call → message


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can-tools/ -->

# CAN frame tool and downloads

Build or inspect a frame using the command definitions of this manual's firmware release. All calculations
run in your browser; the tool does not connect to an adapter or send commands to hardware.

## Downloads

[Command definitions (JSON)](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/assets/can/protocol-V108.json) · [Position DBC](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/assets/can/protocol-V108-position.dbc) · [Velocity DBC](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/assets/can/protocol-V108-velocity.dbc) · [Current DBC](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/assets/can/protocol-V108-current.dbc)

The JSON includes the firmware tag, source commit, message IDs, every documented layout and its bit order.
The DBC files cover **nodes 0 to 13**, with both the clean and fault-bit identifiers of driver replies.
Reserved commands are omitted. Values use the firmware's native units: ticks, ticks/s, mA and the units in
the [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/).

Choose the DBC for the `Send_data_pack_1` layout your host sends:

| File | Command layout |
|---|---|
| Position DBC | 8 bytes: position, speed feedforward, current feedforward |
| Velocity DBC | 5 bytes: speed, current feedforward |
| Current DBC | 2 bytes: current |

The three layouts share a CAN identifier. DBC cannot select a layout from the frame's length, so load the
matching file; the browser decoder below handles all three lengths. Other message layouts are the same in
each download.

An RTR request uses the same identifier as its data reply. DBC describes the **data reply**; it does not
represent the request's RTR flag or the empty gripper status poll. Both are supported by the browser tool.

The gripper's two object-detection bits have an unusual order: bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit.
The DBC signal `gripper_object_detection_raw` retains the wire value and supplies text labels (raw 2 =
object while closing, raw 1 = object while opening). The browser decoder converts that pair to the firmware's
numeric status (1 = closing, 2 = opening).

## Try a frame

The example `0x07A`, data `C8 1E 01 2C C0`, is a command to gripper node 0: position 200, speed 30,
current 300 mA, activate and action set, E-stop and release direction clear. These are an illustration of the
encoding; the device's current and motion limits still apply. Select another message above the fields to build
one of its documented forms. To inspect a reply, enter its identifier and data bytes below.

<div class="can-tool" data-schema="../../assets/can/protocol-V108.json" markdown="0">
  <p class="can-tool__status" role="status">Loading the firmware's command definitions…</p>
  <fieldset><legend>Build a frame</legend>
    <label for="ct-node">Node ID (0–13)</label><input id="ct-node" name="node" type="number" min="0" max="13" step="1" value="0">
    <label for="ct-command">Message and layout</label><select id="ct-command" name="command"></select>
    <label><input name="error" type="checkbox"> Driver reply has an active fault (error bit 1)</label>
    <div class="can-tool__fields"></div>
    <button type="button" name="build" class="md-button md-button--primary">Build frame</button>
    <pre class="can-tool__built" aria-live="polite"></pre>
    <button type="button" name="use" class="md-button">Use this frame in the decoder</button>
  </fieldset>
  <fieldset><legend>Decode a frame</legend>
    <label for="ct-id">CAN identifier (hex)</label><input id="ct-id" name="identifier" type="text" value="0x07A" spellcheck="false">
    <label for="ct-data">Data bytes (hex, up to eight)</label><input id="ct-data" name="data" type="text" value="C8 1E 01 2C C0" spellcheck="false">
    <label><input name="remote" type="checkbox"> Remote request (RTR; no payload)</label>
    <button type="button" name="decode" class="md-button md-button--primary">Decode frame</button>
    <div class="can-tool__decoded" aria-live="polite"></div>
  </fieldset>
  <noscript>Enable JavaScript for the frame tool, or use the reference tables and downloads above.</noscript>
</div>

**Check:** the example decodes to the values above. Change the identifier to `0x1FA` to see the same command
addressed to node 3. An invalid length or out-of-range field produces an explanation instead of a frame.

For wiring, termination, host timing and recovery, use [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/can/). To look up a
message's purpose and accepted lengths, use the [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/ -->

# CAN protocol

CAN 2.0, 1 Mbit/s, 11-bit identifiers. The identifier carries the node ID (bits 10 to 7, 0 to 15), the command ID
(bits 6 to 1, 0 to 63) and, in frames from the driver, the error bit (bit 0). [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/can/)
explains how the pieces are used; this page lists them.

Three kinds of message:

- **Send_…** — the host sends data to the driver. A few are answered (the motion commands with
  Respond_data_pack_1, the gripper command with Respond_Gripper_data_pack); most are not.
- **Send_Respond_…** — the host asks for data with a **remote frame** (RTR bit set, no data) under the command ID;
  the driver answers with a data frame under the same command ID.
- **Respond_…** — frames only the driver sends.

Multi-byte values are big-endian (data[0] first); floats are IEEE 754 single precision; bits inside a byte are
numbered from the most significant bit (bit 7 first).

## Every message

| ID | Message | Direction | Length | Group |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [Send_ESTOP](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/system/#send_estop) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 1 | [Send_Clear_Error](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/system/#send_clear_error) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 2 | [Send_data_pack_1](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/motion/#send_data_pack_1) | host → driver | 2, 5, 8 | Motion |
| 3 | [Respond_data_pack_1](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/motion/#respond_data_pack_1) | driver → host | 8 | Motion |

| 5 | [Respond_data_pack_2](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/motion/#respond_data_pack_2) | driver → host | 0 | Motion |

## By group

- [Motion](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/motion/): the motion commands and their answers, HALL homing
- [Gains and limits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/gains-and-limits/): the loop gains, the limits, Kt
- [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/status/): temperature, voltage, identity, errors, current, encoder, Kt, the heartbeat
- [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/system/): node ID, E-stop, idle, save, reset, clear, watchdog, heartbeat setup, settings
- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/gripper/): the gripper command, calibration and the gripper state

Every message the host can send has a method of the same name in `Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN`, listed in
[Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/python/).

## Tools and downloads

[Build or decode a CAN frame, and download this firmware's JSON and DBC definitions](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can-tools/).

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/motion/ -->

# Motion

The commands that move the motor and the frames that come back.

### Send_data_pack_1

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 2</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">2 or 5 or 8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_data_pack_1()`</span></div>

The motion command. Its length decides the control mode the driver enters: 8 bytes command a position with a speed and a current feedforward, 5 bytes a speed with a current feedforward, 2 bytes a current. Send 0 for a feedforward you do not use. A frame of any other length is ignored (the driver flags it as a wrong data length) but still answered.

**8 bytes** — position setpoint with speed and current feedforward (position mode)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2 |  | Position setpoint | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks |
| 3-5 |  | Speed feedforward | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks/s |
| 6-7 |  | Current feedforward | signed 16-bit | mA |

**5 bytes** — speed setpoint with current feedforward (velocity mode)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2 |  | Speed setpoint | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks/s |
| 3-4 |  | Current feedforward | signed 16-bit | mA |

**2 bytes** — current setpoint (current mode)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | Current setpoint | signed 16-bit | mA |

The driver answers with **Respond_data_pack_1**.

Every form resets the watchdog. With `Rstint` set, the integral accumulators are cleared on each new setpoint.

---

### Send_data_pack_PD

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 4</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_data_pack_PD()`</span></div>

Puts the driver in impedance (PD) mode and sets the position, speed and current feedforward of the PD loop, whose gains are KP and KD (Send_PD_Gains).

**8 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2 |  | Position setpoint | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks |
| 3-5 |  | Speed setpoint | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks/s |
| 6-7 |  | Current feedforward | signed 16-bit | mA |

The driver answers with **Respond_data_pack_1**.

Firmware 106 and older wrote the speed into the feedforward instead of the PD loop's speed setpoint, so the speed term had no effect; 107 fixed it.

---

### Send_data_pack_HALL

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 31</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_data_pack_HALL()`</span></div>

Homing against a sensor: the driver spins at the given speed until the input on the ADDITIONAL2 pin shows the trigger condition, then latches the position it reached as its position setpoint and holds it. Sending the command again while the driver is already in HALL mode does not re-arm it; leave the mode first.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2 |  | Speed | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks/s; the sign gives the direction |
| 3 |  | Trigger | unsigned 8-bit | 0 = trigger when the pin is low, 1 = when it is high, 2 = on any edge |

The driver answers with **Respond_data_hall**.

Firmware 103 read only bit 7 of byte 3 (0 or 1); the edge trigger (2) came later.

---

### Respond_data_pack_1

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 3</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span></div>

The driver's answer to Send_data_pack_1 and Send_data_pack_PD: where the motor is, how fast it turns and the current it draws. The Python library stores them as `position`, `speed` and `current`.

**The frame** (8 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2 |  | position | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks |
| 3-5 |  | speed | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks/s |
| 6-7 |  | current | signed 16-bit | Iq in mA |

---

### Respond_data_hall

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 32</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span></div>

The driver's answer to Send_data_pack_HALL: the position and the state of the sensor input. Python attributes: `position`, `HALL_trigger`, `additional_pin2`, `hall_index`.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2 |  | position | signed 24-bit | encoder ticks |
| 3 | 7 | HALL_trigger | bit | 1 while the driver waits for the trigger, 0 once it triggered and holds |
| 3 | 6 | additional_pin2 | bit | the raw level of the ADDITIONAL2 pin |
| 3 | 5 | hall_index | bit | 1 once the trigger has been seen (latched) |

---

### Send_data_pack_2

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 6</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">not implemented</span></div>

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

---

### Send_data_pack_3

# Gains and limits

The commands that set the loop gains and the limits. None of them is answered; save with Send_Save_config.

### Send_PD_Gains

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 16</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_PD_Gains()`</span></div>

Sets KP and KD, the gains of the impedance (PD) loop. Keep them with Send_Save_config.

**8 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | KP | float 32 |  |
| 4-7 |  | KD | float 32 |  |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Current_Gains

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 17</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Current_Gains()`</span></div>

Sets Kp and Ki of the PI current loops (Iq and Id).

**8 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Kp_iq | float 32 |  |
| 4-7 |  | Ki_iq | float 32 |  |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Velocity_Gains

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 18</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Velocity_Gains()`</span></div>

Sets Kp and Ki of the PI velocity loop.

**8 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Kpv | float 32 |  |
| 4-7 |  | Kiv | float 32 |  |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Position_Gains

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 19</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Position_Gains()`</span></div>

Sets Kp of the P position loop.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Kpp | float 32 |  |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Limits

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 20</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">8 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Limits()`</span></div>

Sets the speed limit and the current limit the loops may reach. The current limit is clamped by the firmware to the driver's maximum of 2800 mA.

**8 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Speed limit | float 32 | encoder ticks/s |
| 4-7 |  | Current limit | float 32 | mA |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Kt

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 22</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Kt()`</span></div>

Sets the motor's torque constant Kt, which the driver uses to estimate torque from current.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Kt | float 32 | Nm/A |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Voltage_Limit

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 34</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Voltage_Limit()`</span></div>

Sets the voltage limit of the current loops (the same value as `#Vlim`), in mV. 0 means use the supply voltage. Added in firmware 105.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Voltage limit | signed 32-bit | mV; 0 = Vbus |

The driver does not answer this command.

# Status requests

Data the host asks for with a remote frame (RTR bit set, no data); the driver answers with a data frame with the same command ID. And the heartbeat, which the driver sends on its own.

### Send_Respond_Ping

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 10</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Ping()`</span></div>

Asks the driver to answer with an empty frame, to see that it is on the bus.

**The frame** (0 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Ping**.

---

### Send_Respond_Temperature

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 23</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Temperature()`</span></div>

Asks for the thermistor temperature. Meaningful only with the thermistor enabled (`#Term 1`).

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | temperature | signed 16-bit | °C |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Temperature**.

---

### Send_Respond_Voltage

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 24</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Voltage()`</span></div>

Asks for the supply voltage.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | voltage | unsigned 16-bit | mV |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Voltage**.

---

### Send_Respond_Device_Info

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 25</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Device_Info()`</span></div>

Asks for the driver's identity: hardware version, batch date and serial number from the EEPROM, and the firmware release (from firmware 105 on this is the build's own version; before, a value from the EEPROM).

**The frame** (7 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | HARDWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | PCB revision |
| 1 |  | BATCH_DATE | unsigned 8-bit | production batch |
| 2 |  | SOFTWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | firmware release, e.g. 108 |
| 3-6 |  | SERIAL_NUMBER | unsigned 32-bit | serial number |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Device_Info**.

---

### Send_Respond_State_of_Errors

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 26</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()`</span></div>

Asks for every error flag and the calibrated, activated and watchdog states.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 7 | error | bit | any error is active |
| 0 | 6 | temperature_error | bit | motor over the temperature limit |
| 0 | 5 | encoder_error | bit | magnet not detected or misaligned |
| 0 | 4 | vbus_error | bit | supply voltage outside the limits |
| 0 | 3 | driver_error | bit | the MOSFET driver reports undervoltage, thermal shutdown or overcurrent |
| 0 | 2 | velocity_error | bit | speed over the limit |
| 0 | 1 | current_error | bit | reserved; never set by this firmware |
| 0 | 0 | estop_error | bit | Send_ESTOP was received |
| 1 | 7 | calibrated | bit | the motor is calibrated |
| 1 | 6 | activated | bit | the controller is activated |
| 1 | 5 | watchdog_error | bit | the watchdog ran out |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_State_of_Errors**.

---

### Send_Respond_Iq_data

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 27</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Iq_data()`</span></div>

Asks for the measured Iq current.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | current | signed 16-bit | mA |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Iq_data**.

---

### Send_Respond_Encoder_data

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 28</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Encoder_data()`</span></div>

Asks for the position and the filtered speed, as 32-bit values. Python attributes `position` and `speed`.

**The frame** (8 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | position | signed 32-bit | encoder ticks |
| 4-7 |  | speed | signed 32-bit | encoder ticks/s |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Encoder_data**.

---

### Send_Respond_Kt

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 33</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Kt()`</span></div>

Asks for the torque constant Kt the driver uses. Added in firmware 105.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Kt | float 32 | Nm/A |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Kt**.

---

### Respond_Heartbeat

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 9</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span></div>

The frame the driver sends on its own at the heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup); empty. Off by default. Any other frame the driver sends resets the heartbeat timer, so a driver that answers motion commands at a high rate never sends a heartbeat.

**The frame** (0 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/system/ -->

# System

Identity, saving, resetting, errors, the watchdog, the heartbeat and the settings.

### Send_CAN_ID

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 11</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_CAN_ID()`</span></div>

Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). Setting the ID also sets the bootloader's board ID. The driver answers to the new ID at once; the ID is kept over a power cycle only after Send_Save_config.

**1 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | ID | unsigned 8-bit | 0 to 15 |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_ESTOP

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 0</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_ESTOP()`</span></div>

Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Idle

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 12</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Idle()`</span></div>

Puts the driver in idle mode (the motor coasts or brakes, see Send_Settings).

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Save_config

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 13</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Save_config()`</span></div>

Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag) to the EEPROM.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Reset

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 14</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Reset()`</span></div>

Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Clear_Error

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 1</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Clear_Error()`</span></div>

Clears the error flags and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Watchdog

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 15</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Watchdog()`</span></div>

Sets the watchdog: every valid CAN frame the driver receives resets it; when the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and stops. 0 turns it off (the default). The action byte is stored but not acted on by this firmware: the driver always stops into its idle behaviour.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Time | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |
| 4 |  | Action | unsigned 8-bit | 0 idle, 1 hold, 2 brake (stored only) |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Heartbeat_Setup

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 30</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()`</span></div>

Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Interval | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |

---

### Send_Settings

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 35</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span></div>

Sets boolean settings that have no command of their own: a mask byte says which settings the frame touches, a value byte gives their new values; settings outside the mask are left alone. Bit 0 is the idle behaviour: 1 brake (phases shorted), 0 coast. Added in firmware 108 (Spectral Micro 107). The Python library has no call for it yet.

**2 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Mask | unsigned 8-bit | bit 0 = write the idle behaviour |
| 1 |  | Value | unsigned 8-bit | bit 0: 1 brake, 0 coast |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Cyclic_command

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 29</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">not implemented</span></div>

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/can/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

The commands of gripper mode (`#Gripper 1`, saved).

### Send_gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 61</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 or 5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_data_pack()`</span></div>

The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1 |  | Speed | unsigned 8-bit | 0 slowest, 255 fastest |
| 2-3 |  | Current | signed 16-bit | current limit of the move in mA; not clamped by the firmware, see the gripper manual for the safe range |
| 4 | 7 | Activate | bit | 1 activate the gripper, 0 deactivate |
| 4 | 6 | Action | bit | 1 go to the position, 0 idle |
| 4 | 5 | E-stop | bit | 1 raises the gripper E-stop error |
| 4 | 4 | Release direction | bit | read by the firmware but not used |

The driver answers with **Respond_Gripper_data_pack**.

---

### Send_gripper_calibrate

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 62</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_calibrate()`</span></div>

Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Respond_Gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 60</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span></div>

The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated`.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | gripper_position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1-2 |  | gripper_current | signed 16-bit | measured current in mA |
| 3 | 7 | gripper_activated | bit | 1 activated |
| 3 | 6 | gripper_action_status | bit | 1 going to the position, 0 idle, auto-release or calibrating |
| 3 | 5-4 | gripper_object_detection | 2 bits | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | 3 | gripper_temperature_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 2 | gripper_timeout_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 1 | gripper_estop_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 0 | gripper_calibrated | bit | 1 calibrated |

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/ -->

# UART commands

Every command the firmware release this site describes understands over the serial port. The kind, the argument
type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the descriptions are written by
hand. [Over UART](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/06-operation/uart/) explains the protocol.

## Syntax

```
#<Name> [number]
```

- A **Set/Get** command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
- A **Get** command only prints.
- An **Action** command does something; a number after it is ignored.
- Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the number at most 19; the line ends with LF (CR before it is
  fine). 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
- A name the parser does not know is answered `Unknown command`.

## Every command

| Command | Kind | Argument | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`#Activate`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Brake`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Action |  | Motion |
| [`#Cal`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Action |  | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#Calangle`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Action |  | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#Calibrated`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | int | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#Calpwr`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | float | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#CANID`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Cbw`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | float | Gains and limits |
| [`#Clear`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Close`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Action |  | Motion |
| [`#Coast`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Action |  | Motion |
| [`#Cyc`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Cyca`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Default`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Dir`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | int | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#Error`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Flux`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | float | Calibration and motor parameters |

| [`#Gripact`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripcal`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/) | Action |  | Gripper |
| [`#Gripcur`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripinfo`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/) | Get |  | Gripper |
| [`#Gripper`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Grippos`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripstop`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripvel`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#HALL`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Action |  | Motion |
| [`#Help`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |

| [`#KP`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | float | Gains and limits |
| [`#Kpid`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | float | Gains and limits |
| [`#Kpiq`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | float | Gains and limits |
| [`#Kpp`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | float | Gains and limits |
| [`#Kpv`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | float | Gains and limits |
| [`#Kt`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | float | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#KV`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | float | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#L`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | float | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#LED`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Magnet`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Get |  | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#microstep`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Set/Get | int | Motion |
| [`#Mode`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |

| [`#Openloop`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Set/Get | float | Motion |
| [`#Opens`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | float | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#Openv`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | int | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#P`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Set/Get | int | Motion |
| [`#Param`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |

| [`#PDV`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Set/Get | int | Motion |
| [`#Phase`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Get |  | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#PP`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | int | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#Pullconfig`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#PWM`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#R`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | float | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#Reset`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Resv`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | int | Calibration and motor parameters |
| [`#Rstint`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | int | Gains and limits |
| [`#Save`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#SERNUM`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#stepinterval`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Set/Get | int | Motion |
| [`#Temp`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Term`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Tlim`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Ud`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Set/Get | int | Motion |
| [`#Uq`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Set/Get | int | Motion |
| [`#V`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/) | Set/Get | int | Motion |
| [`#Vbus`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Vlim`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | int | Gains and limits |
| [`#Vlimit`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/) | Set/Get | int | Gains and limits |
| [`#Vmax`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Vp`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/) | Set/Get | int | Calibration and motor parameters |

The parser also accepts `#EN`, `#SIN`, `#SPWM`, `#Vmin`, `#flux`, `#zz`, which have no handler: the driver answers nothing to them.

## By group

- [Motion](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/): setpoints and modes
- [Gains and limits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/): the loop gains, the limits, the integrator reset, the current loop bandwidth
- [Calibration and motor parameters](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/): `Cal`, the motor's R, L and pole pairs, the constants calibration finds, the calibration settings
- [Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/): save, reset, defaults, identity, errors, temperature, the cyclic output
- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/): gripper mode

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/motion/ -->

# Motion

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Iq` | Set/Get | float: current setpoint in mA | Current (torque) control with the given Iq setpoint. Enters **current** mode. | the measured Iq in mA |
| `#Id` | Set/Get | float: current setpoint in mA | Sets the Id setpoint; normally left at 0. | the measured Id in mA |
| `#V` | Set/Get | int: speed setpoint in encoder ticks/s | Velocity control with the given speed. Enters **velocity** mode. | the measured speed in ticks/s |
| `#Uq` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | Voltage-torque mode with the given q-axis voltage (no current loop). Enters **voltage torque** mode. | the Uq setpoint in mV |
| `#Ud` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The d-axis voltage used in voltage-torque mode; does not change the mode. Enters **voltage torque** mode. | the Ud setpoint in mV |
| `#Brake` | Action |  | Goes to idle with the motor braking (phases shorted); also the idle behaviour from then on. Enters **idle** mode. | `Brake 1` |
| `#HALL` | Action |  | Homing against the sensor on ADDITIONAL2 at 3000 ticks/s (see Send_data_pack_HALL for the CAN form with a chosen speed and trigger). Enters **HALL** mode. | `HALL` |
| `#Coast` | Action |  | Goes to idle with the motor coasting (phases open); also the idle behaviour from then on. Enters **idle** mode. | `Coast 0` |
| `#P` | Set/Get | int: position setpoint in encoder ticks | Position control to the given position. Enters **position** mode. | the measured position in ticks |
| `#PD` | Set/Get | int: position setpoint in encoder ticks | Impedance (PD) control around the given position with the gains KP and KD. Enters **PD** mode. | the measured position in ticks |
| `#PDV` | Set/Get | int: speed setpoint in encoder ticks/s | The speed setpoint of the PD loop. | the PD speed setpoint |
| `#PDI` | Set/Get | int: current feedforward in mA | The current feedforward of the PD loop. | the PD current feedforward |
| `#Idle` | Action |  | Goes to idle; the motor coasts or brakes as set by Brake / Coast. Enters **idle** mode. | `Idle` |
| `#Close` | Action |  | Leaves open loop and goes back to closed-loop idle. Enters **idle** mode. | nothing |
| `#microstep` | Set/Get | int: microsteps per full step | The microstepping used by gosteps. | the microstep setting |
| `#stepinterval` | Set/Get | int: step time | The time between steps for gosteps. | the step interval |
| `#gosteps` | Set/Get | int: number of steps (sign = direction) | Moves the given number of steps open loop, with the timing of stepinterval and microstep. Enters **open-loop steps** mode. | `Moving for N steps` |
| `#Openloop` | Set/Get | float: electrical speed | Spins the motor open loop, as a plain stepper, with the voltage set by Openv. Enters **open loop** mode. | the open-loop speed |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gains/ -->

# Gains and limits

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Vlimit` | Set/Get | int: speed in encoder ticks/s | The speed limit; the velocity integrator is clamped to it. | the current limit |
| `#Vlim` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The voltage limit of the current loops (Ud and Uq); 0 means use the supply voltage. | the current limit in mV |
| `#Kpp` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the position loop. | the current value |
| `#KP` | Set/Get | float: gain | KP of the impedance (PD) loop. | the current value |
| `#KD` | Set/Get | float: gain | KD of the impedance (PD) loop. | the current value |
| `#Kpv` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the velocity loop. | the current value |
| `#Kpiq` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the Iq current loop; also sets Kpid. | the current value |
| `#Kpid` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the Id current loop. | the current value |
| `#Kiv` | Set/Get | float: gain | Ki of the velocity loop. | the current value |
| `#Kiiq` | Set/Get | float: gain | Ki of the Iq current loop; also sets Kiid. | the current value |
| `#Kiid` | Set/Get | float: gain | Ki of the Id current loop. | the current value |
| `#Ilim` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The Iq current limit. Set it to the rated phase current of your motor; the firmware clamps it to 2800 mA. | the current limit |
| `#Cbw` | Set/Get | float: bandwidth in Hz | The current loop bandwidth calibration uses to compute Kpiq and Kiiq. | the bandwidth |
| `#Rstint` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Whether the integral accumulators are reset on every new setpoint. | the setting |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/calibration/ -->

# Calibration and motor parameters

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#R` | Set/Get | float: resistance in Ω | The phase resistance of the motor (one coil). STEPFOC does not measure it; enter the datasheet value before Cal. | the current value |
| `#L` | Set/Get | float: inductance in H | The phase inductance of the motor (one coil); enter the datasheet value before Cal. | the current value |
| `#Kt` | Set/Get | float: Nm/A | The torque constant, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#KV` | Set/Get | float: rpm/V | The velocity constant, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#Flux` | Set/Get | float: Wb | The flux linkage, found by calibration. Not reachable over UART: the parser accepts `#flux` (lowercase) but the handler expects `Flux`, so neither spelling works. | the current value |
| `#Cal` | Action |  | Runs the calibration routine (see Motor parameters and calibration). Enter R, L and PP first. | the calibration log |
| `#Calangle` | Action |  | Runs only the angle-offset step of the calibration. Enters **angle-offset calibration** mode. | `Idle` when done |
| `#Offset` | Set/Get | float: angle in rad | The angle offset between encoder zero and electrical zero, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#Iqoffset` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The current used by the angle-offset search. | the current value |
| `#Magnet` | Get |  | Reads the encoder's magnet status. | `Magnet Good` or `Magnet Bad` |
| `#Dir` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The counting direction of the encoder (1 is the default). | the current value |
| `#Phase` | Get |  | Prints the phase order found by calibration. | `Phase order is: N` |
| `#Resv` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The voltage calibration starts the resistance test at (not used by STEPFOC, which does not measure resistance). | the current value |
| `#Calpwr` | Set/Get | float: power in W | The power calibration may dissipate in the resistance and inductance tests (not used by STEPFOC). | the current value |
| `#Openv` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The voltage of the open-loop spin, in calibration and with Openloop. | the current value |
| `#Opens` | Set/Get | float: electrical speed in rad/s | The speed of the open-loop spin in calibration. | the current value |
| `#Vp` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The voltage of the phase-order search in calibration. | the current value |
| `#Calibrated` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The calibrated flag. `#Calibrated 1` clears a calibration error without calibrating; the motor may still be uncalibrated. | the flag |
| `#PP` | Set/Get | int: pole pairs | The motor's pole pairs: 50 for a 1.8° stepper, 75 for 1.2°, 100 for 0.9°, 125 for 0.72°. Calibration accepts only these values. | the current value |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/utility/ -->

# Status and utility

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Vmax` | Set/Get | int: voltage in mV | The supply voltage above which a Vbus error is raised. | `Vmax in mV: N` |
| `#Save` | Action |  | Writes the configuration to the EEPROM. Do it after calibration and after tuning. | `Save` |
| `#Reset` | Action |  | Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again. | nothing |
| `#Tlim` | Set/Get | int: temperature in °C | The temperature at which the temperature error is raised; 75 by default. | `Temp limit N` |
| `#Default` | Action |  | Writes the factory defaults to the EEPROM, including the serial number, hardware version and batch date, and clears the gripper flag, heartbeat and watchdog. Back those up first. | `Loaded default config!` |
| `#Temp` | Get |  | Prints the thermistor temperature. | °C, or `Temp Off` while the thermistor is disabled |
| `#Term` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Enables the thermistor measurement and the temperature error (off by default). | the setting |
| `#Mode` | Get |  | Prints the control mode. | `Idle mode`, `Position control`, `Speed control`, `Current control`, `PD control`, `Open loop`, `Gripper mode` |
| `#Vbus` | Get |  | Prints the supply voltage. | mV |
| `#Error` | Get |  | Prints which errors are active. | `No errors!` or `In error state!` followed by one line per active error |
| `#Clear` | Action |  | Clears the errors and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; a calibration error is cleared only by calibrating (or `#Calibrated 1`). Enters **idle** mode. | `Clear errors` |
| `#Iabc` | Get |  | Prints the phase currents. | `Ia`, `Ib` in mA |
| `#PWM` | Get |  | Prints the PWM duty values. | the duties |
| `#Help` | Action |  | Prints a short command reference. Added in firmware 108. | the reference |
| `#Info` | Get |  | Prints the driver's identity and state: hardware and firmware version, serial number, motor parameters, calibration, errors. | the report |
| `#Param` | Get |  | Prints every gain of every loop. | the gains |
| `#Cyc` | Set/Get | int: interval in ms (0 = off) | Sends position, speed and Iq on its own every interval: `$ <position> <speed> <Iq>`; for BetterSerialPlotter. | `Cyclic disabled` when turned off |
| `#Cyca` | Set/Get | int: interval in ms (0 = off) | Like Cyc, in the Arduino plotter format `Position:x,Speed:y,Iq:z`. | `Cyclic disabled` when turned off |
| `#CANID` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 13 | The CAN node ID. Use 0 to 13: the firmware accepts 14 and 15, but the bootloader reserves them and a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN. Setting the ID also sets the bootloader's board ID. Kept over a power cycle after Save. | the ID, or `Invalid CAN ID` |
| `#SERNUM` | Set/Get | int: number | The serial number stored in the EEPROM. | `Serial number is: N` |
| `#Activate` | Action |  | Sets the activated flag. | `Controller activated` |
| `#Pullconfig` | Get |  | Prints the whole configuration on one line, for Motor GUI. | the configuration |
| `#LED` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Turns the status LED on or off. | the LED state |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/108/reference/uart/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Gripper` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Whether this driver is a gripper. Save it; `#Default` clears it. | the flag |
| `#Gripcal` | Action |  | Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Enters **gripper calibration** mode. | `Gripper calibration!` |
| `#Gripinfo` | Get |  | Prints the gripper state: calibrated, activated, end stops, position, current. | the report |
| `#Gripstop` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The gripper E-stop bit. | the bit |
| `#Gripact` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The activate bit. | the bit |
| `#Gripcur` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The current limit of gripper moves. The firmware does not clamp it; see the gripper manual for the safe range. | the setpoint |
| `#Gripvel` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 255 | The speed setpoint of gripper moves. | the setpoint |
| `#Grippos` | Set/Get | int: 0 (open) to 255 (closed) | The position setpoint; also activates the gripper, sets the action bit and goes to gripper mode. Enters **gripper** mode. | the current position |
